back2basics.text: Coal is a major source of energy in India, used primarily for power generation and industrial fuel. Coal production involves extracting coal from mines, while overburden removal is the process of clearing soil and rock above coal seams to access the coal. Offtake refers to the quantity of coal supplied to consumers. Efficient coal production and supply are critical for maintaining energy security, reducing imports, and supporting industrial growth.

body.label: Exceeded targets
body.text: WCL achieved 102.47% of its coal production target, 108.82% of its offtake target, and 104.56% of its overburden removal target from April to October 2026.

body.text: WCL reduced pithead coal stock from 13.034 MT on April 1, 2026 to 4.44 MT on October 31, 2026, liquidating around 8.6 MT or 66% of opening stock.

body.label: Technology upgrades
body.text: WCL operates six Surface Miners and three Continuous Miners, improved transportation infrastructure, rapid loading systems, and automated weighbridges.

body.label: Quality focus
body.text: About 86% of coal samples from April to October met declared grade, and overloading charges were significantly reduced.

sections.heading: What operational and technological measures supported WCL’s performance?

back2basics.text: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is the regulator for securities markets in India. It enforces rules to prevent insider trading, which involves trading based on unpublished price-sensitive information. Listed companies must maintain a structured digital database of persons who have access to such information to ensure transparency and prevent misuse. SEBI uses orders, warnings, and recovery certificates to enforce compliance and protect investors.

back2basics.concept: Public Accounts Committees and Democratic Dissent
back2basics.text: Public Accounts Committees (PACs) are parliamentary committees responsible for examining government expenditure to ensure it complies with legislative approval and promotes accountability. Democratic dissent refers to the right and practice of expressing disagreement within a democracy, which helps bring new ideas, correct errors, and improve governance. Both PACs and dissent are essential for a functioning parliamentary democracy, ensuring transparency, accountability, and inclusive decision-making.

2026-11-02-pm-dabd1f4c6b.deck: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla inaugurated the Conference of Chairpersons of Public Accounts Committees (PACs) in Thiruvananthapuram on 3 November 2026, emphasizing the evolving role of PACs in audit and accountability. He also called on lawmakers to uphold dissent as a democratic strength during the Haryana Vidhan Sabha's Janpratinidhi Sammelan on 2 November 2026.

back2basics.text: Satellite navigation systems use a constellation of satellites that transmit signals with precise timing and location data. mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about ISRO's GSLV-F18 mission and NavIC system:
1. The GSLV-F18 mission successfully placed the NVS-03 satellite into Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit, enhancing NavIC's navigation capabilities.
2. The NVS-03 satellite carries only imported atomic clocks for timing accuracy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because NVS-03 carries an indigenously developed atomic clock alongside procured ones, not only imported clocks.

body.label: Mission success
body.text: ISRO launched the GSLV-F18 on 30 October 2026, placing the NVS-03 satellite into a precise Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit from Sriharikota.

body.label: Satellite purpose
body.text: NVS-03 is the third of five next-generation NavIC satellites designed to improve India's regional satellite navigation system's coverage, accuracy, and reliability.

body.label: Navigation signals
body.text: The satellite carries navigation payloads in L1, L5, and S frequency bands, enhancing NavIC's compatibility and coverage over India and 1,500 km beyond.

body.label: Indigenous technology
body.text: NVS-03 includes an indigenously developed atomic clock for precise timing, essential for accurate positioning.

body.label: Launch vehicle details
body.text: GSLV-F18 is a three-stage vehicle with an indigenous cryogenic upper stage, marking the 20th flight of the GSLV series.

sections.heading: What was the GSLV-F18 mission and its objectives?

body.label: Strengthening NavIC
body.text: The mission supports India's independent Positioning, Navigation, and Timing capabilities, reducing reliance on foreign systems.

body.label: Strategic and civilian use
body.text: NavIC provides open positioning services for civilians and encrypted services for strategic users.

body.label: Technological self-reliance
body.text: Use of indigenous cryogenic technology and atomic clocks enhances India's space sovereignty and technological capacity.

body.label: Applications
body.text: NavIC supports transportation, maritime, aviation, disaster management, and precision agriculture.

sections.heading: Why does the GSLV-F18 mission matter for India's space capabilities?

body.label: Launch failures
body.text: ISRO experienced two PSLV launch failures in the last 18 months, affecting mission frequency and reliability.

body.label: Slow mission pace
body.text: GSLV-F18 was only the second successful launch in 2026, indicating a slow recovery for the national space programme.

body.label: Resource constraints
body.text: ISRO faces shortages in human and material resources, impacting its ability to meet ambitious plans like human spaceflight and reusable launch vehicles.

body.label: Procurement bottlenecks
body.text: Difficulties in obtaining specialised components and vendor readiness have delayed satellite projects like NavIC.

body.label: Need for reforms
body.text: Experts recommend increased budget allocation, dedicated NavIC operators, and a national space law to address private participation and liability.

wayForward.label: Increase budget and resources
wayForward.text: The government should raise the Department of Space budget to around ₹17,000 crore to enhance manufacturing, satellite replacement, and recruitment.

wayForward.label: Dedicated NavIC operator
wayForward.text: A separate operator for NavIC is needed to allow ISRO to focus on core space missions.

wayForward.label: National space law
wayForward.text: India requires a legal framework addressing private sector participation and liability in space activities.

whyInNews.text: On 30 October 2026, ISRO launched the GSLV-F18 mission successfully, placing the NVS-03 satellite into Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit to enhance NavIC, after a period of constrained launches due to previous failures.
